source_text:
Ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ κολαζόμενος πλούσιος, καὶ ὁ
ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ πένης ἀναπαυόμενος, πρὸ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Σωτῆρος καὶ πρὸ
τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λεγόμενοι ὁ μὲν ἐν
ᾅδου κολάζεσθαι, ὁ δὲ ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ ἀναπαύεσθαι, διδάσκουσιν ὅτι καὶ νῦν τῇ
ἀπαλλαγῇ σώματι χρῆται ἡ ψυχή. Ἐκ τῶν Μεθοδίου.
thought_title: The rich man and Lazarus teach that the soul now uses a body
orientation: Origen is arguing that the parable of Lazarus and the rich man shows the soul uses a body even now, before the resurrection.
pass_a_gloss: But also the rich man being punished, and the poor man resting in Abraham's bosom, before the coming of the Savior and before the end of the age, and because of this before the resurrection, being said the one to be punished in Hades, the other to rest in Abraham's bosom, teach that even now at the departure the soul uses a body. From the works of Methodius.

bible_refs.note: ὁ κολαζόμενος πλούσιος, καὶ ὁ ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ πένης ἀναπαυόμενος

pass_b_english: Consider the rich man being punished and the poor man resting in Abraham's bosom. Both are described as being in these states before the coming of the Savior and before the end of the age, and therefore before the resurrection. The one is punished in Hades, and the other rests in Abraham's bosom. They teach us that even now, at its departure, the soul uses a body.
